Title: Attempt to upload a photo with both userId and workerId provided simultaneously
Preconditions: A valid authenticated user session is established
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/v1/photos/upload with a multipart file payload containing both userId and workerId parameters set to valid numeric IDs

Test Data: multipartFile: [binary image data], userId: 123, workerId: 456
Expected Result: The system returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request status code with an error message indicating that a photo can only be associated with either a user or a worker, not both. The photo is not stored.

Title: Attempt to update an existing photo to have both userId and workerId simultaneously
Preconditions: An existing photo record exists in the system associated with either a user or a worker
Steps:
1. Send a PUT request to /api/v1/photos/{photoId} with a multipart file payload containing both userId and workerId parameters set to valid numeric IDs

Test Data: multipartFile: [binary image data], userId: 123, workerId: 789
Expected Result: The system returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request status code with an error message indicating that a photo can only be associated with either a user or a worker, not both. The existing photo remains unchanged.

Title: Authenticate user with valid username and password credentials
Preconditions: An active user account with username 'admin' and password 'admin' exists in the system.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with an Authorization header formatted as 'Bearer <jwt-token>' and a response body containing user details including id, username 'admin', email, and role list.

Title: Create a new geographical area with a unique name
Preconditions: The user is authenticated with an administrator account assigned the ROLE_ADMIN role.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response containing a JSON body with status 'success', message 'Area created successfully', and the created Area entity containing a generated ID and name 'Downtown Dhaka'.

Preconditions: An area with ID 1 exists in the system, and the user is authenticated with administrative privileges.

1. Send a POST request to /api/areas/1/shops with the payload in testData.

Test Data: {
  "shopName": "Master Tailors",
  "shopPhone": "+8801700000000",
  "geoLocation": "23.8103,90.4125",
  "ownerName": "John Doe",
  "username": "mastertailor",
  "email": "shop@example.com",
  "address": "123 Main St",
  "areaId": 1,
  "status": true
}
Expected Result: HTTP 201 Created response containing the created Shop entity with a generated ID, shopName 'Master Tailors', and areaId 1.

Title: Add a worker to an existing shop
Preconditions: A shop with ID 1 exists in the system, and the authenticated user has ownership permissions for shop ID 1.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/1/workers with the payload provided in testData.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Worker Joe",
  "phone": "+8801800000000",
  "address": "456 Side St",
  "shopId": 1,
  "status": true
}
Expected Result: HTTP 201 Created response containing a JSON body with status 'success', message 'Workers added successfully', and the created Worker data object matching shopId 1.

Title: Set account PIN for customer after registration
Preconditions: A user with phone number '01811112233' exists with userType 'customer'.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with boolean result true. User password is stored encoded and role 'ROLE_CUSTOMER' is assigned.

Title: Add a new worker to a shop as shop owner
Preconditions: Shop with ID 5 exists and belongs to the authenticated user.
Steps:

2. Send a POST request to /api/v1/shops/5/workers with the worker JSON payload in testData.
3. Observe the response.

  "name": "Alex Mercer",
  "phone": "01911112233",
  "address": "456 Worker Ave"
}
Expected Result: HTTP 201 Created or 200 OK response containing the created worker object with shopId set to 5 and assigned worker ID.

Title: Upload a profile photo associated with a User ID
Preconditions: User with ID 101 exists in the system. No workerId parameter is provided.
Steps:
1. Prepare a multipart/form-data POST request to /api/v1/photos.
2. Include an image file, form param 'userId'=101, and leave 'workerId' blank as described in testData.
3. Send the request and verify the outcome.

Test Data: Form-data fields:
- file: sample_profile.jpg (image/jpeg, binary content)
- userId: 101
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response returning saved Photo entity details with userId equal to 101, matching content type, and binary photo data persisted.

Title: Verify application binds to and listens on configured custom port 8083
Steps:
1. Deploy and start the application. 2. Monitor startup logs for server listening port. 3. Send a GET request to http://localhost:8083/api-docs.

Test Data: server.port=8083
Expected Result: Application successfully starts and binds to port 8083. HTTP 200 OK is returned from http://localhost:8083/api-docs.

Steps:
1. Deploy the application with configured spring.datasource properties. 2. Start the application. 3. Execute any database read/write operation.

Title: Verify JWT tokens are validated using configured secret and honor 24-hour expiration duration
Preconditions: jwt.secret set to 'test-secret' and jwt.expirationMs set to 86400000 (24 hours) in properties.
Steps:
1. Authenticate to generate a valid JWT token. 2. Verify token payload expiration claim (exp). 3. Send a request to a protected endpoint using the token.

Test Data: jwt.secret=test-secret, jwt.expirationMs=86400000
Expected Result: Token expiration claim matches 24 hours (86,400,000 ms) from issuance time. Protected endpoint request succeeds with HTTP 200/201.

Title: Verify email dispatch succeeds using Gmail SSL SMTP configuration with 20s timeouts
Preconditions: Valid user action requiring email dispatch (e.g., worker OTP generation).
Steps:
1. Trigger an operation that sends an email (e.g., worker OTP request). 2. Verify logs and recipient inbox.

Test Data: spring.mail.host=smtp.gmail.com, spring.mail.port=465, spring.mail.username=noqueue.club, spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.ssl.enable=true, timeouts=20000
Expected Result: Email is sent successfully over SSL port 465 without connection timeout or authentication failure.

Title: Verify Swagger UI and OpenAPI JSON documentation are accessible at custom paths
Preconditions: Application running with configured springdoc properties.
Steps:
1. Open browser/HTTP client and request GET http://localhost:8083/swagger-ui.html. 2. Request GET http://localhost:8083/api-docs.

Test Data: springdoc.swagger-ui.path=/swagger-ui.html, springdoc.api-docs.path=/api-docs
Expected Result: Swagger UI page loads successfully at /swagger-ui.html and valid OpenAPI JSON specification is returned at /api-docs.

Title: Verify appointment buffer time setting of 5 minutes is applied during scheduling
Steps:
1. Attempt to schedule two consecutive appointments with a 5-minute gap. 2. Attempt to schedule two appointments with less than a 5-minute gap.

Test Data: appointment.buffer.time.minutes=5
Expected Result: Appointments with at least 5 minutes gap are accepted; overlapping or insufficient buffer appointments are rejected.
